spec_match.rationale: Accurately depicts the documented change — Chrome-umbrella attribution vs per-App-Shim name/icon with per-app Settings/Focus control — using clearly-labelled illustrations (real OS output is impossible from a page), the verified flag id from about_flags.cc (enable-mac-pwas-notification-attribution → features::kAppShimNotificationAttribution, kOsMac), and the enterprise MDM/bundle-ID caveat from the chromestatus entry.

interactive.rationale: PWA-name/title/body inputs re-render both illustration cards live (name, initial, uppercase attribution line, aria-label), and the this-device row runs real platform + display-mode probes rather than static text.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index promises editable before/after illustrations plus exact enable steps; the page delivers both plus the device-capability table.

edge_cases.rationale: Covers non-macOS, macOS-tab, and enterprise-policy cases in the table, and empty-input placeholders; it does not illustrate macOS dark-mode rendering or the per-app permission prompt sequencing, which are cosmetic but would deepen the comparison.

references.rationale: Links https://chromestatus.com/feature/5863296436666368 and the Notifications spec; enable steps cite about_flags.cc as the flag-id source.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite's manual assertion records exactly this page's OS-visual contract with its full prerequisite list, keeping the unautomatable part honestly blocked rather than faked.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 verified: both illustration cards render inside dashed ILLUSTRATION frames, status line states both attributions and the simulated-rendering disclaimer, this-device row shows NO with platform Linux reasoning, console clean, 0 overflow at true 360; typing into the inputs was not machine-driven (render() output was verified from its on-load run).

telemetry_health.rationale: attr-compare-illustration-labelled asserts both illustration labels exist (the page's core honesty invariant) and attr-compare-device-honest asserts the device verdict matches the real probes.

design_system.rationale: Mock cards use variables (accent-blue/emerald icons with ivory text, AA), the illustration frames use accent-rose dashed borders with rose label text on paper (AA for its size/weight), inputs on bg-ivory with black text.

accessibility.rationale: Labelled inputs, mock cards exposed as role=img with meaningful aria-labels that update with the PWA name, captions carry the semantic difference in text, aria-live status confirms updates.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified at 1280x1800 (cards side by side) and true 360 (cards stack, inputs full-width, steps wrap via code overflow-wrap): 0px horizontal overflow, all controls reachable.

guidanceConsulted.query: responsive control panel narrow mobile no horizontal overflow
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Use auto-fit minmax grids with min-width:0 children so paired panels stack cleanly on narrow viewports.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: mock-grid and the controls grid both use repeat(auto-fit,minmax(...,1fr)) with min-width:0; measured 0 overflow at true 360.

guidanceConsulted.query: labelled text inputs live preview mobile
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Explicit label elements bound to inputs, adequate touch height, and immediate feedback on input.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: All three fields use wrapping label[for] with 2.75rem min-height inputs and an input-event live re-render confirmed by an aria-live status.

guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Illustrative composites should expose a single accessible name describing their meaning rather than their internal text soup.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Each mock banner is role=img with an aria-label naming the attribution ('Simulated macOS banner attributed to …') that updates live; captions carry the detail as real text.

openQuestions.title: Verify the illustrations against real macOS Notification Center output
openQuestions.detail: A human on macOS Chrome 130+ with the flag and an installed PWA should compare the mock cards' structure (attribution line, icon position) against real banners and adjust the illustration or captions if the real layout differs materially.

openQuestions.title: Drive the input-edit path in an automated browser run
openQuestions.detail: Headless verification confirmed the on-load render and live status; a CDP- or MCP-driven run should type a new PWA name and assert both cards and aria-labels update, closing the last untested interaction.

summary: Editable, clearly-labelled before/after illustrations of the attribution change with the verified flag id, complete enable steps including the enterprise MDM caveat, and a device-capability table whose this-device row uses real probes (Linux → NO). Verified on desktop and true-360 mobile with clean console and zero overflow; real-OS visual comparison remains a manual macOS task.
